title: Winter tree: tapered branching with snow ridges only on thick limbs
note: Snow sits on branches thick enough to hold it and trunks taper from a real base; coating every twig reads as spray.
intent: Bare winter trees oscillate between "coarse low-poly stubs" and "thin noisy twigs" when the brief is adjectives; the fix is a shape rule, not a magnitude. Taper: 3–4 levels, each level cutting the radius sharply (the skills say by ≥ 70%; halving from a ≥ 0.12 trunk keeps exactly the two thickest levels above the snow floor) and spawning 2–3 children (not 6–8), no child longer than 1.5× its parent, so heavy first- and second-order limbs dominate the silhouette and terminal twigs are the minority; trunk radius ≥ 0.12 world units at the base or the whole tree collapses into "pale sticks". Snow is ridges — small flattened spheres or elongated boxes — only on branches whose radius ≥ 0.04 units; terminal twigs stay bare, because a white coating on the finest branches is read as "spray", the #1 rejection trigger. Each snowed branch sags 10–15° below its parent’s axis so the canopy reads weighted rather than as stiff summer foliage.

check.note: Snow ridges sit only on branches of radius >= 0.04 world units (twigs bare) and trunks are >= 0.12 at the base; white coating on the finest twigs is read as spray, thin trunks as pale sticks.

port: Add makeWinterTree(rng) to the vegetation module with the seeded rng, expose userData.radius on trunks and userData.branchRadius on every snow ridge; when a verdict swings between "stubs" and "sticks", pin the taper ratio, children per level and the 0.04 snow floor in the brief instead of any density or size parameter.

evidence.note: utility-pole builds: taper ≥70% per level with 2–3 children, snow ridges only on branches with radius ≥0.04, droop 10–15°, trunk radius ≥0.12 at the base
oscillation stop: fix branch topology (3–4 taper levels, snow only on the two thickest levels, none on sub-3px twigs) before touching density or size
branches must not extend beyond 1.5× their parent length; stray geometry past an anchor fails regardless of silhouette
procedural geometry needs structural grammar: hierarchy depth, branches per level, taper ratio, accumulation rules and thickness range
